identity.title: Zapotin mitigates breast cancer progression by targeting PKCepsilon mediated glycolytic pathway regulation.

content.abstract: BACKGROUND: The breast cancer recurrence and chemoresistance has increased over the years. A novel PKC, PKCepsilon, may promote chemoresistance by causing hypoxia and cancer metabolic rewiring. A natural flavonoid, Zapotin, in colon cancer cells may modulate PKCepsilon expression. Therefore, this study aimed to explore Zapotin impact on PKCepsilon expression and the metabolic profile of breast cancer cells. METHODS: Pharmacophore analysis of Zapotin was performed and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were employed to study PKCepsilon and Zapotin interaction stability. The effect of Zapotin treatment on PKCepsilon expression and various aspects of cancer cell viability and metabolism was studied in MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cell lines using real-time PCR, growth and death assays, and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry. RESULTS: In silico analyses revealed good solubility and absorption of Zapotin with lower toxicity. Zapotin showed cancer cell-specific cytotoxicity (P < 0.0001). It's treatment also reduced breast cancer cell viability, colony formation, and migratory potential by targeting PKCepsilon and associated HIF-1a and VEGF signaling (P < 0.01). Zapotin also impacted PKCepsilon-mediated metabolic signaling by targeting glycolytic pathways. CONCLUSION: This study demonstrated the role of PKCepsilon mediated HIF-1a, VEGF, and glycolytic pathways in promoting breast carcinogenicity and demonstrated Zapotin as a potential treatment option for different types of breast tumors.
